content.tldr: Covers the full lifecycle of a staff session: account creation → login → token refresh → logout → deactivation.

workflows.title: New Staff Account Creation
steps: 1. Admin calls POST /api/v1/users with email, password, role, storeId
2. System validates: email uniqueness, role enum, storeId active, password length
3. System hashes password (bcrypt, cost 12)
4. System creates User record, isActive=true
5. System returns sanitised user (no passwordHash)
6. Admin communicates credentials to employee (out-of-band — email, WhatsApp, etc.)
failure_paths: Duplicate email → 409 — admin must use a different email
Inactive storeId → 400 — admin must reactivate store first

workflows.title: Staff Login (Session Start)
workflows.trigger: Staff member opens the app / POS terminal at start of shift
steps: 1. Staff enters email + password
2. Client calls POST /api/v1/auth/login
3. System looks up user by lowercase email
4. System checks isActive=true for user AND store
5. System compares bcrypt hash
6. System creates accessToken (JWT, 15 min) with payload { sub, email, role, storeId }
7. System creates refreshToken (random UUID), stores in Redis key refresh:{userId} with TTL 604800s
8. System returns { accessToken, refreshToken, user }
9. Client stores both tokens securely (memory for accessToken, httpOnly cookie or secure storage for refreshToken)
workflows.success_outcome: Staff is authenticated and can call protected endpoints
failure_paths: Wrong password or unknown email → 401 'Invalid credentials'

workflows.title: Silent Token Refresh
workflows.trigger: Client detects accessToken is expired (exp check before API call, or 401 response)
steps: 1. Client calls POST /api/v1/auth/refresh with refreshToken
2. System looks up Redis key refresh:{userId} decoded from token
3. System verifies token value matches stored value in Redis
4. System checks user is still active
5. System deletes old refreshToken from Redis
6. System issues new accessToken + new refreshToken
7. System stores new refreshToken in Redis with fresh TTL
8. Client replaces both stored tokens
failure_paths: Token not in Redis (expired or rotated) → 401 — client must redirect to login
User deactivated since last refresh → 401 — client clears tokens, redirects to login

workflows.title: Logout (Session End)
workflows.trigger: Staff clicks logout, closes shift, or session is manually terminated
steps: 1. Client calls POST /api/v1/auth/logout with valid accessToken in Authorization header
2. System extracts userId from JWT
3. System deletes Redis key refresh:{userId}
4. System returns 200
5. Client discards both tokens from local storage
failure_paths: Redis key already gone (already logged out) → 200 (idempotent, no error shown to user)

workflows.title: Staff Account Deactivation
workflows.trigger: Employee leaves the business or is suspended
steps: 1. Admin calls PATCH /api/v1/users/:id/deactivate
2. System sets user.isActive=false
3. System deletes Redis key refresh:{userId} (immediate revocation)
4. System returns 200
5. Employee's current accessToken remains valid up to 15-min TTL — accepted risk
workflows.success_outcome: Employee cannot start a new session; current session expires within 15 min
